rollups.text: Academic essay on women’s representation in Montserrat cinema: On March 3, 2024, the user was choosing between essay topics and planned research, an outline, and a first draft by May 15. On April 5, the user finalized the topic as women’s representation in Montserrat cinema from 1990 to 2020; they were analyzing rhetoric and bias in scholarly articles and had an outline that Michele had rated 82% on April 2. The user planned weekday evening writing sessions and aimed for a 90% final grade. By May 9, the draft was 4,200 words; by May 13 it was reported at 4,700 words, above the 4,500-word target. The user submitted the essay on May 15 and celebrated with Shannon on May 16. On July 10, the user received a 92% grade, with argumentation and evidence synthesis praised. Elapsed time from topic selection to grade: 96 days.

Research direction and publication goals: On March 3, 2024, the user was motivated to transition into academic publishing by the end of 2024. On June 1, the user aimed for a 90% essay grade and hoped to publish the essay by August 2024; they also restructured the paper for journal format and added a planned 500-word literature review. After receiving a 92% essay grade on July 10, the user decided to broaden the research from its existing focus to Caribbean-wide film representation. On July 15, the user was considering full-time academic publishing but had not decided. Elapsed time from the initial publishing goal to the reported grade and expanded direction: 129 days.

Montserrat filmmaker interview research: By June 1, 2024, the user intended to interview filmmakers in August about gender portrayal and approved interview questions. Plans varied across conversations: five Montserrat filmmakers were mentioned for qualitative interviews, seven for interviews about gender portrayal, and three Caribbean filmmakers for August fieldwork. A schedule was discussed for interviewing seven filmmakers August 1–15, transcribing by August 20, conducting initial analysis by August 25, and submitting a report September 1; confirmation that this schedule was adopted was not established. Elapsed time from the June 1 planning discussions to the latest stated August/September schedule: up to 92 days.

Conference paper with Greg: On June 1, 2024, the user was balancing a conference paper with Greg, with a June 3 deadline mentioned, and a journal submission due June 5. The user later said the conference paper had been submitted to the Montserrat Media Symposium on July 12. The user planned edits July 16–18 for a July 20 deadline, and the editing period was extended through July 19 to incorporate late feedback. Elapsed time from the June 1 prioritization discussion to the stated July 20 final deadline: 49 days.

Citation and writing software used, considered, or discussed: Zotero—downloaded March 2, 2024; the user reported a library of 45 tagged sources on April 5 and 52 sources on April 5 in a separate record; updated to version 6.0 on May 30. NVivo—installed April 3 after Greg’s suggestion; by April 5 the user reported coding film scripts and a 30% improvement in coding speed. Hemingway Editor—the user began using it for draft clarity on March 3, reported a 25% reduction in passive voice on May 11, and a 35% reduction while assessing a conference paper on July 15. Grammarly Premium—the user compared it with ProWritingAid on March 3 and planned weekly checks beginning May 1. Scrivener—the user switched from Microsoft Word on May 5 and preferred split-screen editing by May 10. EndNote—the user began a free trial around July 6, considered buying it for $250 on July 15, and had heard Carla recommend it on July 5. The user prefers trialing new software before buying.

Recurring academic feedback and support: Carla gave the user feedback on a documentary script after they met at the Montserrat Film Festival on January 15, 2023; reviewed the essay outline at Café La Belle on April 1, 2024; and hosted a celebratory dinner on May 20, where they discussed future research. Robert, the user’s 75-year-old retired-professor mentor, shared a 1985 gender-studies essay over Zoom on April 4, 2024, reviewed the user’s essay draft on May 9, and encouraged the user on June 1. Michele, the user’s instructor, rated the outline 82% on April 2 and led a counterargument workshop on May 8. Heather, whom the user met in an online writing course, exchanged drafts with the user weekly; on May 7 she advised adding statistical evidence. Greg met the user at a University of Montserrat seminar on February 20, 2024, and planned joint media-influence research with the user.

Citation-style changes across projects: The user adopted APA 7th edition on April 3, 2024, for the essay, confirmed by Michele. On May 28, the user adjusted a manuscript to MLA style to follow journal guidelines. On July 15, the user said they had adapted the conference paper to Chicago style for a symposium held July 11. These styles were associated with different works and do not establish a single permanent change in preference.

Essay word-count progress: The user’s target was 4,500 words. By May 9, 2024, the user had written 4,200 words; by May 13, the draft was reported at 4,700 words, 200 words above target. The reported increase from 4,200 to 4,700 words was 500 words over four days.

Reported writing-process improvements: By April 5, 2024, NVivo use had improved the user’s coding speed by 30%. On April 5, tagged Zotero sources were reported to improve source-retrieval speed by 40%. On May 11, the user reported reducing passive voice by 25% with Hemingway Editor; on July 15, they reported a 35% reduction in a conference paper. The passive-voice figures refer to separate reports and may concern different drafts.

Academic grade changes and targets: Michele rated the user’s essay outline 82% on April 2, 2024. The user aimed for 90% on the final draft, and on July 10 reported receiving 92%, a 10-percentage-point increase from the outline score and 2 points above the final-grade target.

Writing-tool preference changed for the essay: On March 3, 2024, the user preferred Microsoft Word to Google Docs for formatting control. On May 5, the user switched from Word to Scrivener to organize the essay draft; by May 10, the user preferred Scrivener’s split-screen mode for editing and note-taking.
